---
name: iphone-duo-stock-check
description: >-
  Use when someone wants to know whether the iPhone Duo (or another hard-to-find
  iPhone) is in stock at Apple Stores near them, or wants to be alerted when it
  comes back.
---
# iPhone Duo stock check

The iPhone Duo is Apple's foldable iPhone and is very hard to find. Your job is to tell the owner, fast and honestly, whether it's in stock at their watched Apple Stores, and to alert them the moment it shows up.

## What to know (from memory, ask only if missing)
- Their postal or ZIP code, country, and time zone. Postcodes vary by country (letters, spaces, and digits), so don't treat them as 5-digit ZIPs.
- Their watched stores: up to 5 Apple Stores, saved in memory.
- Exact model: colour and storage, read from Apple's buy page for their country, plus carrier only where it matters (see Model choices).
- Any backup configurations they said are OK.
- Their alert window and where alerts go (this chat or an X DM).

If none of this is saved yet, run the iphone-duo-finder-getting-started skill instead of asking piecemeal.

## What the check covers
Apple's pickup check shows whether you can order online and pick up at a store. It doesn't show walk-in stock, so say that when it matters. If the buy page shows the Duo as a pre-order, or only a "Ships [date]" status, tell the owner that pickup stock may not show up until it's in stores.

## Getting to the pickup check (browser)
Use a browser on your computer with Apple's buy page. Don't use Apple's internal or undocumented endpoints (for example curl calls to pickup-message URLs), even if they look faster.
1. Open the iPhone Duo buy page for their country (for example apple.com/shop/buy-iphone/iphone-duo in the US, apple.com/ca/..., apple.com/uk/..., apple.com/au/... elsewhere).
2. Choices unlock in order: colour, storage, trade-in, payment, carrier (only where Apple sells by carrier), AppleCare. Choose "no trade-in" and full price. If a colour or storage button doesn't respond to clicks, select it with the keyboard (Tab to the option, then Space or Enter). Ignore stray US carrier wording on non-US pages.
3. Press "Check availability" (it's in the page's bottom bar). Type the postal or ZIP code, then click the suggestion that appears. Pressing Enter alone may do nothing.
4. Read the result:
   - If there's a store list (sometimes behind a "Not available today at N nearest stores" link), expand it and read each watched store's own row.
   - If Apple only shows a summary like "Not available today at N nearest stores" with no list, count that as a no for each watched store that's among those N nearest. Check any watched store that isn't, by entering its own postcode.
5. Stop before adding anything to the bag. Never order or reserve without the owner's yes.

## Finding nearby stores
Apple's pickup dialog is the main source. It usually lists the nearest Apple Stores (5 to 12 seen so far) with distances in the unit Apple shows (km or mi), so use that unit. The order can be a little off, so sort by distance. If Apple shows no list or no distances, use a stock tracker for that country that lists stores with distances (in the US, ManzanaTracker's stock page for the ZIP). Apple's distances are straight-line, so say driving is longer. Use the store name as the area, and get a street address from the store's apple.com/retail/<store> page if needed. Apple's retail list and locator pages show no distances, can fail to load, and can include far-off stores, so treat them as backup only.

**Reasonable reach** is about 100 km / 60 mi, roughly an hour's drive. If no store is within that range, show the nearest 2 or 3 with distances, say they're far, and ask whether to watch them anyway. If only some are within reach, watch those and say so.

## Picking or changing stores
Use this when the owner gives a new postal or ZIP code or asks to change stores. During first setup, the getting-started skill already asks this, so don't ask it twice.
- Ask with a question card: "Pick the closest 5 for me" or "I'll choose my stores".
- **Pick for me:** take the 5 closest stores within reasonable reach.
- **I'll choose:** show up to 10 of the closest, with distances, in a multi-select card and let them pick up to 5. If they pick more than 5, ask which 5 to keep.
- Tell them the final list with each store's name and distance, save it with the code to memory, and update the restock-watch routine's prompt if one exists.

## Model choices
Read the colours, storage sizes, and prices from the country's buy page, and quote prices in the local currency as Apple shows them. Options differ by country, so don't rely on memory. Ask about carrier only where Apple sells by carrier (in the US: AT&T, T-Mobile, Verizon, or "Connect to any carrier later", which is unlocked). Where Apple sells unlocked or SIM-free only (for example Canada, the UK, and Australia), skip the carrier step and say so.

## How to check
1. **Apple's own pickup check is the source of truth.** Use the exact configuration and read each watched store's status as above. If Apple says no iPhone Duo models are available for pickup today at nearby stores, that covers every configuration, so you don't need to check the backups separately. If anything is available, check the exact model and each backup. Report Apple's pickup wording as shown (for example "Currently unavailable" or "Available today").
2. **Cross-check a public stock tracker that covers the owner's country.** Use ManzanaTracker for the US (switch it to the iPhone Duo, since it opens on another model), and InStock Radar or PickupAlert for the UK and Australia. For other countries, do a quick web search for an iPhone Duo stock tracker there, and skip this step if none turns up. Name the tracker you used, say it can be a few minutes behind, and convert any times it gives into the owner's time zone.
3. Never invent stock. If a page wouldn't load or blocked you, say which one.

## How to report
- Lead with the answer: in stock at a watched store or not.
- For each watched store that has it, give the store name, the configuration, Apple's pickup text, the price, and a link to buy or reserve.
- If nothing is in stock, say so plainly and include Apple's current delivery date if shown (for example "Ships 22 Jan") as the fallback. Give a restock pattern only if a tracker you opened reports one, name the tracker, and give the time in the owner's zone. Never claim a pattern no tracker reported.
- Give times in the owner's time zone, labelled.

## Restock alerts
Read the routines skill, then create one restock-watch routine. Write the watched stores, the postal or ZIP code, the exact model, the backups, and the alert destination into its prompt so each run is self-contained.
- **Usual restock hours:** set the window from what a tracker for the stores' country reports (for example, US trackers have reported about 10 AM to 1 PM ET, and a UK tracker about 6 AM UK time). Start about 2 hours before the earliest reported time and end about 2 hours after the latest, convert to the owner's time zone, and write that as the cron, every 5 minutes (for example `*/5 8-14 * * *`). If no tracker reports a pattern, use `*/5 8-15 * * *` (8 AM to 4 PM local). Apple doesn't publish restock times, so call it a best guess and offer around the clock as the safer choice.
- **Around the clock:** `*/5 * * * *`. Five minutes is the fastest a routine can run.
- **Each run:** do a quick pickup check for the watched stores only. When a matching configuration (or an accepted backup) shows up, alert the owner right away, naming the store, the configuration, and a buy link. Stay completely quiet when nothing changed.
- **Where alerts go:** by default, a message in this chat, which reaches them as an app notification. If they chose an X DM and their X account is connected through the X plugin, also send the alert as a DM to their own X account. Only ever DM the owner. SMS needs a texting connector, so offer to connect one if they ask.
- **No repeat alerts:** after alerting, note the store, configuration, and time in the journal. Don't alert again for that store and configuration until a later run has seen it sold out and it comes back.
- **If checks run slow:** if a check regularly takes longer than 5 minutes or Apple starts blocking it, widen the schedule to every 10 or 15 minutes and tell the owner once.
- Tell the owner alerts are near real time: a slot can sell out between checks, so they should order as soon as they're pinged. Pause or delete the routine once they've bought one.

## Buying
If the owner wants you to grab it, confirm the exact store, configuration, carrier if any, and price first, then follow the purchases skill. Apple may limit how many each customer can buy.

skills.content:
---
name: iphone-duo-finder-getting-started
description: >-
  Use for the first conversation with a new owner of the iPhone Duo stock finder
  bot, to set up their search and restock alerts.
---
# Getting started (4 quick steps)

Say hi in one short line: you watch up to 5 Apple Stores near them and ping them the moment an iPhone Duo is available for pickup there. Tell them setup takes 4 quick steps. Ask one step at a time, use tap-to-answer question cards wherever there are set options, and keep each message short.

**Step 1: Location.** Ask for their postal or ZIP code. Accept any country's format, with letters, spaces, or digits. Work out the country and time zone from it, and ask only if it's unclear.

**Step 2: Stores.** Get the nearest Apple Stores with distances, as the iphone-duo-stock-check skill describes, and use the unit Apple shows.
- If no store is within reasonable reach (about 100 km / 60 mi), show the nearest 2 or 3, say they're far (and that Apple's distances are straight-line), and ask whether to watch them anyway.
- Otherwise ask with a question card: "Pick the closest 5 for me" or "I'll choose my stores". For pick for me, take the 5 closest within reach and list them. For I'll choose, show up to 10 of the closest, with distances, in a multi-select card and let them pick up to 5. If they pick more than 5, ask which 5 to keep.

**Step 3: Model.** Read the colours, storage sizes, and local prices from Apple's buy page for their country, then ask with question cards for colour and storage, showing each price as Apple does. Ask about carrier only where Apple sells by carrier (the US). Where it's unlocked or SIM-free only, skip it and say so. Finish with a multi-select card for any backup configurations they'd accept, including "No backup, exact model only". If the page shows the Duo as a pre-order or only a ship date, mention that pickup stock may not appear until it's in stores.

**Step 4: Alerts.** Ask two quick question cards:
- When to watch: "Usual restock hours (<window>)", filled in from the stock-check skill's restock rule in their time zone, or "Around the clock". Mention that Apple doesn't publish restock times, so the shorter window is a best guess.
- Where to ping them: "Here in this chat (app notification)" or "Also as an X DM to me". Only offer the X DM option when their X account is connected through the X plugin, and otherwise offer to connect it. If they ask for text messages, explain that SMS needs a texting connector and offer to set one up.

Then, without more questions:
1. Save the postal or ZIP code, the time zone, the stores, the model, the backups, the alert window, and the alert destination to memory.
2. Run a first stock check with the iphone-duo-stock-check skill and send the result.
3. Create the restock-watch routine exactly as that skill's Restock alerts section describes.
4. Confirm in one line that it's running, when it checks, and where alerts will come.

Let them know they can change stores, model, alert hours, or where alerts go any time just by asking.
